milestones.title: Redesign — paper first
milestones.description: The concept canvas (six boards) built for real: type wall, family page, your-own-text flow, selection and drag, Pairing Studio, motion. Gate: every board matched by eye at 1440×900 in both themes; e2e, a11y and the 60 fps wall budget green.

milestones.title: Match by letters
milestones.description: Find fonts by the shape of their distinctive letters: named traits computed from the outlines (R leg straight or curved, O round, g single- or double-storey …) as filter chips, a Letters wall preset that shows only the glyphs you care about, and later per-glyph similarity ('an R like this one'). Gate: trait detectors ≥ 90 % against the labelled corpus, search stays under 50 ms, the first scan stays under 10 s.

milestones.title: After the designers' test
milestones.description: What the first designers at WMG hit in a week of use: families not legible as families, icons and the activation dot too small, a toolbar that changes shape per view, a Layout mode that shows one font, a Characters section that does not scale and clips descenders, a Sources screen that looks like a form, and no way to browse by foundry. Boards 9–11 on the concept canvas are the targets.

milestones.title: Launch
milestones.description: Everything that must be right before the first public release of Font Fu. E54 is part one; more pre-launch epics will follow.

epics.title: Redesign foundation: targets, fixture, tokens, motion primitives
epics.summary: What every redesign story builds on: the concept boards exported as target images next to the code, a browser-mode library big enough to look like one, the owner's accent per theme, and the motion tokens and transition helpers the later epics reuse. Concept canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/4EtzdBCYU4LWsxaXNQKvNv — boards 1–6. The design rules live in dev-docs/redesign/DESIGN.md.

stories.title: Export the six concept boards as target images
criteria: dev-docs/design/redesign/ holds the 18 PNGs listed in its README.md (five wall presets, eight family-page states, two your-own-text states, drag, studio, motion), each exported from the concept canvas at 1440 px wide with the Export-state tweak set as the README says; the export date is filled in
Every UI story in E41–E46 links its target image by that path; a story is reviewed against the image, not against the previous screenshot
DESIGN.md's audit section is replaced by a pointer to the boards and a short list of what the boards leave open (dark theme of each board, compact density, narrow windows)

stories.title: Browser-mode library that looks like a library
criteria: `?mockLibrary=wall` (and the default for e2e @screens) serves 60 families across classifications: ≥12 serif, ≥16 sans, 6 slab, 6 script/hand, 6 mono, 8 display, 6 variable (two with 3+ axes), with Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese coverage on some and deliberate gaps on others, 3 duplicates and 2 broken files — all from fixtures/fonts/ (OFL/Apache/UFL only)
Families carry realistic designer, foundry, year, licence and style counts; mock `sampleTexts` reports `missing` glyphs for the gap families so tofu rendering can be seen
scripts/redesign/shots.mjs and the @screens spec use the wall library by default; the three-family library stays available as `?mockLibrary=small` for the existing specs that count rows
No change to the FmClient interface or generated types

stories.title: Accent per theme and on-accent token
criteria: `--fm-accent` is #C56EB2 in light and #AB4B96 in dark; a new `--fm-on-accent` is #141413 in light and #ffffff in dark; both pairs ≥ 4.5:1, enforced by styles/contrast.test.ts

Every element that paints text on the accent (primary button, count badge, pressed chip, toast, switch label if any) uses `--fm-on-accent`; accent-coloured text and links go back to `--fm-fg` — grep shows no `color: var(--fm-accent)` on text
Focus ring, selection ring, active segment, switch-on state, slider thumb and the activation toggle take the accent
The @screens set opened in both themes; axe (a11y.spec.ts) green

stories.title: Motion tokens, reduced-motion switch and transition helpers
criteria: theme.css defines `--fm-motion-fast: 120ms`, `--fm-motion-move: 200ms`, `--fm-motion-page: 280ms`, `--fm-ease: cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1)` and sets all three durations to 0ms under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`; no component declares its own duration or curve (lint rule or grep test)

`src/motion/` exports `useReducedMotion()`, a `<FmFade>` / `<FmSlide>` pair over Vue `<Transition>`, a `<FmFlipGroup>` over `<TransitionGroup>` that animates transform only, and `withViewTransition(fn)` that uses `document.startViewTransition` when present and falls back to running `fn` directly
Only `transform` and `opacity` are animated by the helpers (asserted in a unit test that inspects the generated styles)
Board 6 (6-motion.png) is copied into dev-docs/redesign/MOTION.md as the table the later epics implement against

epics.title: Type wall — the library as designers open it
epics.summary: Board 1. One hero control (type to preview), a uniform wall of white cards on paper that reflows with the size slider, a quiet paper-tinted sidebar, filters as a button plus chips, no inspector on the wall. Target: dev-docs/design/redesign/1-wall-word.png (and 1-wall-pangram/alphabet/numerals/paragraph.png for the presets).

stories.title: The wall: uniform specimen cards that reflow
criteria: Grid view renders families as white cards on #ffffff with a hairline (`--fm-border`) and 12 px radius: specimen centred (the preview text, never truncated — the text shrinks to fit or the card shows the longest prefix that fits on a word boundary), footer with activation dot, family name (500) and style count / Variable in tabular figures

The size slider (24–120) resizes every visible card and the grid reflows through `<FmFlipGroup>`; cards keep identity; off-screen cards jump; 60 fps with 1,000 families in the wall library (measured in e2e with the Performance API, asserted ≥ 55 fps median)
Column count follows width (minmax 260px); at 1440 px that is four columns; the wall stays virtualised in rows
Selected card: 2 px accent ring; hover: shadow lift per the motion table; Enter opens the family page, Space opens Quick Look, A toggles activation, as today
Matches 1-wall-word.png (and 1-wall-pangram/alphabet/numerals/paragraph.png for the presets) at 1440×900 in light and dark (reviewer compares side by side; differences listed in the PR)

stories.title: Preview text as the hero control
criteria: Above the wall: a 44 px text field 'Type to preview' with a hint at its end, preset chips Word · Pangram · Alphabet · Numerals · Paragraph — each a different wall layout as in 1-wall-<preset>.png (4 columns / 2 wide / 2 wrapped / 4 figures / 2 body-text) — then a divider and a Language picker (recent languages first, then all from `listLanguages()`) that puts that language's pangram on the wall

Typing repaints every specimen on the next frame with no transition; the value is shared by list, wall, waterfall, family page and Quick Look, and remembered per view (view preferences in localStorage, as today)

The size slider applies in every preset, scaled to the preset's density (Word 1×, Pangram 0.6×, Alphabet 0.42×, Numerals 0.75×; Paragraph is fixed at the body size), so a user who likes big specimens gets them everywhere; the preset and size are remembered per view

The old preview toolbar's remaining controls (size, auto size, line height, tracking, alignment, metrics, outline, colours, surface) live in a Preview options popover opened from one button at the end of the row; nothing else is on screen by default
Keyboard: `/` focuses search, `T` (when no row is focused) focuses the preview field; Esc returns focus to the wall

stories.title: Sidebar as a quiet paper panel
criteria: Sidebar background `--fm-surface` (paper tint #f6f5f2 light / surface-2 dark), 232 px, hairline on its right; rows 30 px with a 16 px Lucide icon, label and a right-aligned tabular count; the active row has the 7 % tint
Section headers are 11 px uppercase with their actions as icon buttons that appear on hover/focus (New collection, Add folder, Import set); no text buttons inline in the list
Collections show a colour dot (E44.3) and smart collections a distinct icon, not a trailing 'Smart' pill; Problems appears once, as a section with its count; empty sections show one quiet line
Bottom row: problems count with its dot and the ⌘K/Ctrl+K hint; app/API/platform versions move to About
Matches the sidebar of 1-wall-word.png (and 1-wall-pangram/alphabet/numerals/paragraph.png for the presets); RTL chrome and compact density verified in @screens

stories.title: Filters as a button and a chip row
criteria: The top bar shows `Filters` with a count badge (accent, on-accent text) that opens the existing drawer; active filters render as removable chips to its right, one row, overflow collapses into '+N'
The chip wall above the list is gone from every view; its facets are all reachable in the drawer (parity checked by the filters e2e spec)
The count line above the wall reads '212 families · Sans serif · Serbian (Latin)' and 'Sorted by name · change'

stories.title: No inspector on the wall
criteria: The wall, list, waterfall and table views no longer show the inspector pane; selecting a row shows its name and state in the count line, Enter or a click on the name opens the family page, Space opens Quick Look
The `]` shortcut and the toolbar inspector toggle are removed from these views; the table view keeps its column menu
Every inspector capability has a home on the family page (E42) — a checklist in the PR maps Info/Axes/Features/Glyphs/Developer/License/Palettes/Notes to their new section
The existing inspector e2e specs are updated to the family page; none deleted

epics.title: Family page — one place for everything about a family
epics.summary: Board 2. Clicking a card pushes a page: hero specimen in your text with the variable axes under it, a segmented switch Styles · Text · Characters · Features · Pairings · Info, and a quiet rail (languages you can preview in, pairs well with, facts). Target: dev-docs/design/redesign/2-family-*.png (one per section; see dev-docs/design/redesign/README.md); the board is interactive — play it for every section.

stories.title: Route, push/pop navigation and the page frame
criteria: `/family/:id` route; opening from any view pushes the page with the shared-element transition from the motion table (fallback: slide + fade); Back (button, Esc, Alt+←) pops it and restores the view's scroll position and selection

Top bar: ‹ Library, '1 of 212 · ← → next family' (arrows move to the previous/next family in the current filtered order without leaving the page), icon buttons Favorite · Add to collection · Tag · Find similar, and the primary 'Activate family' (accent, on-accent)
Page skeleton: hero area, axis row, section switch (`UiSegmentedControl`), a 560+ px main column and a 320 px rail that wraps under it below 1100 px

Switching sections replaces only the panel under the segmented switch (120 ms crossfade); the hero, the axis row and the rail stay where they are, so a weight or language chosen on the hero carries across every section
Deep link works in browser mode for the @screens scene `family`

stories.title: Hero specimen and live axes
criteria: Hero: the preview text at 132 px (clamped to the width, one line, ellipsis) in the family's default face; a meta line with foundry, year, axes/style count, licence and activation state

For a variable family every axis is a slider with a numeric readout; dragging updates the hero, the Styles rows and the rail samples on the same frame via `font-variation-settings`; ticks under the weight slider mark the named instances and a label reads '= Medium' within ±12 or 'between instances'
Dragging horizontally on the hero specimen scrubs the weight axis (pointer capture; 1 px = 2 units; Shift halves); the cursor shows ew-resize
'Pin 537 as my instance' calls the existing `pinInstance` and the new style appears in Styles; 'Copy CSS' puts `font-variation-settings` on the clipboard via `cssValues`

stories.title: Styles: named list and weight ramp
criteria: Named styles: one row per face — name and weight/italic meta (150 px), the preview text at 38 px, hover actions Copy CSS · Compare, and an activation switch (`role=switch`, accent when on) that calls activate/deactivate for that face

A `Named styles · N | Weight ramp` switch (variable families only) shows the weight axis at every 100 with the instance name where one exists; clicking a ramp row sets the hero weight; the accent ring on both lists follows the current hero weight (±12)

For families with more than the weight axis the ramp switch offers one ramp per axis (Weight · Optical size · Soft …), nine steps across the axis range, weight first; the other axes hold the hero's current values while one is ramped
Pinned instances (`listVirtualStyles`) appear in the named list with a 'yours' badge and can be deleted from the row menu
Keyboard: ↑/↓ move between rows, Space toggles activation, Enter sets the hero to that row's weight

stories.title: Text section: the reading test
criteria: Three columns of the same passage at 12 / 17 / 24 px labelled captions · body · lead, line height 1.45, `opsz` set to the size where the family has the axis
Measure (40–90 ch) and leading (1.10–1.80) sliders apply to all three; a Paper | Ink switch flips the section to light-on-dark; an ink block below shows the body size on `--fm-fg` ground
The passage is the user's preview text when it is longer than 80 characters, otherwise the stock passage; the Paragraph preset from E41.2 lands here

stories.title: Characters section: grid, blocks and glyph detail
criteria: A 12-column glyph grid from `listGlyphs` in the family's face at 26 px, virtualised, with block filter chips (count per block) and a search that accepts a character, `U+017D` or a glyph name (`getGlyph`)

Selecting a cell (click, arrows, Enter) shows the detail card: the glyph at 160 px, name, code point, 'in N of M styles', and its alternates rendered live (stylistic sets and axis extremes from `GlyphDetail`); Copy glyph and 'Compare with…' (existing GlyphCompare)
No inner scrollbars: the grid grows with the page; the detail card is sticky on tall windows
Matches the Characters state of board 2

stories.title: Features section: off and on, side by side
criteria: Each non-automatic feature from `FeatureInfo` is a row: friendly name with the tag in mono under it, the sample rendered without the feature (muted) and with it (`font-feature-settings`), and a switch
Switched-on features apply to every preview on the page (hero, Styles, Text) through the shared preview state; 'Copy CSS for N switched on' writes the `font-feature-settings` line

Samples are chosen per feature from data/features (E42.11): ligature words for `liga`/`dlig`, mixed case for `smcp`/`c2sc`, digits for `onum`/`tnum`/`pnum`/`lnum`, fractions for `frac`; stylistic sets fall back to the preview text
Rare tags (cvXX, locl, mark…) sit behind an 'N more' expander

stories.title: Pairings section: candidates from your library
criteria: Four to eight cards from `suggestPairings`, each a mini layout — this family as the headline (30 px) over the candidate as body (14 px) — with the candidate's name and its `reasons` joined by ' · '
A `This family for headlines | for body` switch sends the role to the request and swaps which face plays which part in the cards
Clicking a card opens the Studio with the pairing loaded (E45.2); hovering lifts the card per the motion table
Empty state when the library has no candidate: one line and an action to browse catalogs

stories.title: Info section: design, licence, files, metrics
criteria: Four groups in a two-column grid: Design (designer, foundry · year, classification, axes with ranges, named styles, description), Licence (name, 'You may' and 'You may not' lines from `LicenseInfo.permissions`, the user's record with a link to declare), Files (format, location, added, health), Metrics (units/em, cap, x-height with ratio, ascender, descender)
Metrics show an 'Hxg' specimen at 96 px with dashed accent lines at cap height and x-height and a solid baseline, drawn from the face's metrics
Hash, name IDs, vendor ID and the full table list stay in the Developer section, reachable from a 'Technical details' expander at the end of the rail

stories.title: The rail: preview in a language, pairs well with, facts
criteria: 'Supports N languages': only complete languages from `faceCoverage` as chips (six, then '+N more' expands); clicking a chip sets the page's preview text to that language's pangram (`LanguagePreset.pangram`) and marks the chip with the accent; clicking again or 'back to my text' restores the user's text
Under the chips a 22 px line of the language's distinctive glyphs (from data/charsets) rendered in the face — never a fallback font (missing glyphs would be tofu per E43.4)
'Pairs well with': the top two from `suggestPairings` with one reason each and 'Open in Pairing Studio'
Facts grid: designer, foundry, licence with web/embed marks, format/files/size, 'Used in' linking to collections that contain the family; 'Technical details' expander at the end
Choosing a language here also offers 'Show only fonts that can do Polish' which applies the language filter when going back to the wall

stories.title: Language samples: distinctive glyph lines per language
criteria: data/charsets/<lang>.json gains an optional `sampleGlyphs` string (the language's distinctive letters, e.g. 'Šđčćž' for sr-Latn, 'Ąćęłńóśźż' for pl) and the schema and validation test accept it; the 30 most used presets are filled
`LanguagePreset` gains `sampleGlyphs?: string | null` (additive, `#[serde(default)]`); `pnpm gen:types` output committed
Pangrams exist for every preset that has `sampleGlyphs` (data/pangrams); missing ones added for sr-Latn, sr-Cyrl, hr, bs, sl, mk

stories.title: Feature catalog: friendly names, groups and samples
criteria: data/features/features.json (schema-validated) lists every registered OpenType feature tag with a friendly name, a group (Ligatures · Capitals · Figures · Fractions · Positioning · Stylistic · Language · Automatic) and a sample string; the fm-core feature reader uses it for `FeatureInfo.name` and gains `group` and `sample` (additive fields)
A unit test checks every tag the fixture corpus exposes has a name; `cvXX`/`ssXX` without a font-supplied name fall back to 'Character variant 3' / 'Stylistic set 1'
`pnpm gen:types` output committed

stories.title: Licence permissions summary in fm-core
criteria: `LicenseInfo` gains `permissions?: LicensePermissions | null` with `may: string[]`, `mayNot: string[]`, `source: 'open-license' | 'declared' | 'embedding-bits'` — derived in fm-core from the recognised open licence (OFL, Apache, UFL, MIT…), the user's declaration and `fsType`; never invented when nothing is known (null)
Rules live in data/licenses/permissions.json (schema-validated) so wording is editable without code changes
Unit tests cover OFL, Apache-2.0, UFL, a declared desktop licence and a restricted-embedding file
Additive change to fm-api: no existing field renamed or removed; `pnpm gen:types` output committed

stories.title: Role-aware pairing suggestions
criteria: `PairingRequest` gains `role?: 'headline' | 'body' | 'caption'` (default: as today) and `partnerOf?: FaceId` for 'given this body face, suggest headlines'; scoring weights contrast, x-height ratio, width and era differently per role, documented in docs/adr/ as an amendment to the pairing ADR
`PairingSuggestion.reasons` stay plain words and become role-specific ('lower contrast for body', 'x-height within 4 %')
Bench: suggestions for one face against the 10k reference library return in < 50 ms (search budget)
Additive change; `pnpm gen:types` output committed

epics.title: Your own text and honest rendering
epics.summary: Board 3. Type a sentence in your language and the wall becomes reading rows at real body size; fonts that cannot render every glyph say so with visible tofu, and one switch hides them. Target: dev-docs/design/redesign/3-wall-text.png and 3-wall-text-complete.png.

stories.title: Paragraph mode: reading rows when the text is long
criteria: When the preview text exceeds 80 characters or the Paragraph preset is chosen, the wall switches to two-column rows: family name and meta in a 12 px line, the text at the body size (default 17 px / 1.45; the Preview options size applies), 18 px padding, same card chrome
The switch animates as a view crossfade (motion table); switching back restores the wall and its scroll position
The count line reads 'N of M families render your text completely' when the text has glyphs outside Basic Latin
Matches 3-wall-text.png and 3-wall-text-complete.png

stories.title: Script detection for typed text
criteria: `detect_languages(text) -> Vec<LanguageHint { code, confidence }>` in fm-core, exposed through fm-api as `detectLanguages`, using the charsets data: a text whose distinctive glyphs match a preset's `sampleGlyphs`/required set ranks that preset first (sr-Latn before hr before pl for 'đ' + 'ć'); pure ASCII returns an empty list
Unit tests for Serbian Latin, Serbian Cyrillic, Polish, Vietnamese, Greek and mixed text; < 1 ms per call
`pnpm gen:types` output committed

stories.title: Renders-my-text filter with a count
criteria: When the text has non-ASCII glyphs the field's end label reads '<Language> detected · showing fonts that render every glyph' from `detectLanguages`; the count line gets a switch 'Hide the N with missing glyphs' that applies `Supports { kind: 'text' }` to the search
The switch state is a filter chip like any other (removable, shown in the Filters badge count) and is remembered with the view
Performance: toggling on the 1,000-family wall library re-renders in < 100 ms (search budget + paint) measured in e2e

stories.title: Tofu: missing glyphs drawn, never faked
criteria: Every specimen renderer (wall card, list row, waterfall, family hero and rows, Quick Look, Studio) takes the `missing` characters from `sampleTexts` and renders each as an inline box: 0.62 em wide, 1.5 px accent border, 2 px radius, light accent fill; the box is an element with `role=img` and `aria-label="missing glyph ž"`
The row/card shows 'N glyphs missing · š đ č' in the accent colour; the family page shows the same under the hero
No specimen anywhere falls back to a system font for a missing character (a Playwright check compares the rendered width of a known-missing string against the tofu width)
Matches the gap rows of 3-wall-text.png and 3-wall-text-complete.png

epics.title: Selection, drag and collections
epics.summary: Board 4. Select several families, act on them from a bar that rises from the bottom, drag them onto a collection, a tag or the Studio with a ghost and a count, and drag them out of the app as files. Target: dev-docs/design/redesign/4-drag.png.

stories.title: Multi-select model and the selection bar
criteria: Click selects one; Shift-click a range; Ctrl/Cmd-click toggles; dragging on the wall's empty ground draws a box that selects what it touches; Esc clears; Ctrl/Cmd-A selects the filtered set; selection survives view switches
Selected cards/rows: accent ring and a 6 % accent tint; the count line reads 'N selected · Shift-click or drag a box to select · Esc clears'

On the first selection a dark bar (#141413, on it white) rises from the bottom centre per the motion table: 'N families' · Activate · Collection · Tag · Compare · Studio · ×; each action applies to the whole selection through the existing client calls; the bar is a `role=toolbar` reachable with Tab
Matches 4-drag.png minus the drag ghost

stories.title: Drag families onto collections, tags and the Studio
criteria: Dragging a selected card lifts a ghost (the card at 0.9 scale, −3°, shadow, a count badge when more than one) that follows the pointer; the origin cards fade to 35 %

Sidebar collections and tags, and the Studio button in the selection bar, are drop targets: entering one shows the accent ring and the count as '31 → 34'; dropping calls `addToCollection` / `tagFaces` / opens the Studio with the faces; the ghost flies into the row and the count crossfades (motion table)
Smart collections are not drop targets and say why in a tooltip; Esc cancels a drag
Keyboard equivalent exists for every drop (the selection bar's Collection and Tag menus)

stories.title: Collection colours
criteria: `Collection` gains `color?: string | null` (a key from a fixed palette of eight, not a hex) and `createCollection` / `renameCollection` accept it (additive); stored in the database with a migration
The sidebar shows the colour as an 8 px dot before the name and the collection header uses it for its mini specimen strip; the picker is a row of eight swatches in the collection's menu
`pnpm gen:types` output committed; mock supports it

stories.title: Drag out: drop font files into other apps
criteria: Dragging a selection past the window edge starts a native file drag with the faces' files on Windows (IDataObject CF_HDROP), macOS (NSFilePromiseProvider or NSPasteboard file URLs) and Linux (text/uri-list via GTK/Wayland portal) — behind the `FontActivator`-style trait in fm-platform, one implementation per OS, each with an integration test that a second process receives the paths
Files are referenced in place (rule 2: never copied or moved); Explorer/Finder/Nautilus receive them as a copy
Documented in docs/adr/ with the parity decision; a platform that cannot support it ships the feature disabled with a tooltip, not a `cfg` branch elsewhere

epics.title: Pairing Studio — roles on paper
epics.summary: Board 5. One toolbar, the context as a segmented switch, the pairing as four roles in a rail with real font pickers and locks, the page on paper at realistic scale, role marks only on hover or selection, shuffle the unlocked roles, suggestions with reasons, compare two pairings, export. Target: dev-docs/design/redesign/5-studio.png.

stories.title: One toolbar and context presets
criteria: The Studio's four bars become one: Back · 'Pairing Studio' · '<Headline> + <Body> · unsaved' · context switch (Magazine · Web hero · Mobile UI · Video title · Poster) · Compare 2 pairings · Shuffle unlocked · Save · Export

Each context is a real layout from `layoutPresets`/layout templates with the right page: A4 (Magazine, Poster), 1440×900 web hero, 390×844 mobile with iOS type sizes, 1920×1080 video title with safe-area guides
The page sits on a neutral ground (`#ecebe7` light / surface-2 dark) with a soft shadow at 100 % scale by default; the hint line under it says how to hover, select and drag
Matches the toolbar and page of 5-studio.png

stories.title: Roles rail with font pickers and locks
criteria: A 300 px rail lists the context's roles (Magazine: Headline, Deck, Body, Caption; each context defines its own) as cards: role name, lock toggle, a font picker (`UiSelect` with the family rendered in itself and a search over the library), style and size/leading

Role blocks on the page carry no marks at rest; hovering a block shows its role mark in the margin and a hairline ring; clicking selects it (accent ring and mark) and focuses its card in the rail; the rail card's ring follows selection
Drag sideways on a selected block for size, up/down for leading (existing behaviour, kept); Enter edits the block text
Opening the Studio from a pairing card (E42.7) or a drop (E44.2) fills Headline and Body

stories.title: Shuffle unlocked and suggestions with reasons
criteria: 'Shuffle unlocked' asks `suggestPairings` with the locked roles as `partnerOf` and the role as `role`, picks the next candidate for each unlocked role and animates the change (crossfade of the block)
Under the roles a 'Try for <selected role>' list shows three candidates with their reasons; clicking applies to that role only; a shuffled result can be undone (Ctrl/Cmd-Z)
Suggestions come from the user's library only; an empty library state links to catalogs

stories.title: Compare two pairings, save, export
criteria: 'Compare 2 pairings' duplicates the page side by side (two panels, independent roles, shared text); the toolbar label names both; closing one keeps the other
Save stores the pairing as a layout (existing `saveLayout`) named after its faces; History and Revert keep working
Export offers PNG (via E45.5) and PDF (existing print) at 1× and 2×; the file is named '<Headline>-<Body>-<context>.png'

stories.title: Render a layout to PNG in fm-core
criteria: `exportLayoutPng(req: { layout: LayoutId, scale: 1 | 2, surface: 'paper' | 'ink' }) -> path` renders the layout with the core rasterizer (same engine as `renderPreview`), honouring axes and features, into the app's export folder; returns the path
Output matches the webview within tolerance on the fixture layouts (pixel diff < 2 % on a 1× A4 render)
< 1 s for an A4 page at 2× on the reference machine; additive fm-api change; `pnpm gen:types` output committed

epics.title: Motion — everything moves for a reason
epics.summary: Board 6: the twelve moments in dev-docs/redesign/MOTION.md, built on the E40.4 helpers, each with its reduced-motion fallback and a frame budget. Target: dev-docs/design/redesign/6-motion.png.

stories.title: Family page push and pop
criteria: Opening a family: the card's specimen is the shared element that scales into the hero position while the wall fades under it and the top bar crossfades (View Transitions API with `view-transition-name` per card; fallback: 24 px slide + fade), 280 ms `--fm-ease`
Back reverses it at 220 ms with the exit curve and lands on the same scroll position; ← → between families crossfade the page content only (200 ms)
Reduced motion: a 120 ms fade; verified by an e2e test that emulates `prefers-reduced-motion`

stories.title: Wall reflow, view switch and size slider
criteria: Size slider and column-count changes reflow the visible cards with FLIP (transform only), 200 ms; cards entering the viewport appear without animation
Switching view modes crossfades the two lists (200 ms) while the segmented thumb slides (120 ms)

epics.title: Compare — a sheet that grows to the room you need
epics.summary: Board 7. Compare answers 'which of these?' and nothing else: a bottom sheet over the wall that drags from 40 % to full height, Stacked first, a two-up Grid instead of side by side, Overlay kept. Toasts leave the action zone. Targets: dev-docs/design/redesign/7-compare-partial.png, 7-compare-full-grid.png, 7-compare-overlay.png.

epics.title: Match by letters — find fonts by their distinctive glyphs
epics.summary: A designer looks for 'a sans with a straight-legged R and a round O', not for a classification. Three parts, built in this order. (1) Named traits: fm-core reads the outlines of the distinctive letters (R G Q a g e t y M W & 1 7 I l) at the default instance and derives describable properties — R leg straight/curved, O roundness, g and a single/double-storey, G spur, Q tail, t terminal, 1 flag, 7 crossbar, I/l form, M splay, e bar — each with a confidence; rules and labels live in data/classification, results in a glyph_traits table filled by a background pass after the scan; the trigger is the Letters preset itself: the letters you typed are the controls — a letter with traits carries a hairline underline, clicking it opens a picker with the values drawn as glyphs, one value per letter; the choice shows as an ordinary chip. No Letters group in the filter popover, nothing on the cards. Traits are also a CLI flag, a search-box syntax and an MCP argument. (2) Letters: a wall preset that shows only the glyphs you type, large, so the eye does the last step. (3) Later: per-glyph similarity — pick a reference glyph and sort the library by how close each font's version is; the design of (3) is written here so (1) and (2) leave room for it, but it is built after they ship. Board 8 is on the concept canvas; E49.1 exports its three states as dev-docs/design/redesign/8-letters-*.png before the UI stories start.

criteria: dev-docs/design/redesign/ gains 8-letters-wall.png (state = Letters only), 8-letters-picker.png (state = Picker open) and 8-letters-filtered.png (state = Filtered), exported from board 8 at 2× with the Export-state tweak set as the README says; the README table and export date are updated

stories.title: Glyph trait catalog and labelled corpus
criteria: data/classification/glyph-traits.json lists every trait the detectors compute: id ('R.leg'), the glyph (code point), the kind (enum or scalar), the values with friendly labels in en and de ('straight', 'curved', 'both'), a one-line description, and for scalars the thresholds that map to chips ('O.roundness ≥ 0.95 → round'); a JSON schema sits next to it and the data test validates it

The first cut: R.leg {straight, curved, both}; O.roundness scalar (width/height and ellipse deviation); g.storeys {single, double}; a.storeys {single, double}; G.spur {spur, none}; Q.tail {inside, crossing, swash}; t.terminal {flat, angled}; one.flag {flag, none}; seven.bar {bar, none}; I.form {plain, serifed, barred}; l.form {plain, tailed}; M.sides {vertical, splayed}; e.bar {horizontal, angled}

Every enum value carries a small example glyph as an SVG path (stroke-based, 56-unit box) drawn to show that value — these are what the picker displays, so the UI never depends on which fonts the library holds

fixtures/glyph-traits-labels.json hand-labels every trait for at least 50 families of the 200-font fixture corpus (OFL/Apache/UFL only), chosen to cover each value at least five times; a test asserts the coverage so detectors are measured against something real
Traits are defined for Latin only in this cut; the file's shape allows a script field so Cyrillic (Д, Л, б) and Greek can follow without a schema change

stories.title: Outline geometry in fm-core: contours, counters, fits
criteria: `fm-core::glyphs::geometry` loads one glyph's outline at the default instance through skrifa and offers: contour list with winding and bounding boxes, enclosed-counter count, flattening to polylines at a given tolerance, a line fit (max deviation from the chord) for a segment, an ellipse fit (axis ratio and mean radial deviation) for a closed contour, and stem/terminal angle at a point
Composite glyphs, overlapping contours and open contours are handled; a glyph that cannot be parsed returns `None`, never a panic (CLAUDE.md: `Health::Broken`, no `unwrap()` outside tests)
Unit tests on fixture fonts assert known facts (Inter 'O' two contours one counter; a double-storey 'g' two counters; 'l' one contour no counter) and that an empty or malformed glyph is `None`
A benchmark records geometry for the 15 trait glyphs of one face in under 2 ms on the reference machine

stories.title: Trait detectors and the background trait pass
criteria: `fm-core::glyphs::traits` has one detector per trait in E49.2, each returning the value (or scalar) and a confidence 0–1 from the geometry; a detector that cannot decide returns low confidence rather than a guess, and a face lacking the glyph returns nothing for that trait

Accuracy against fixtures/glyph-traits-labels.json is at least 90 % per trait at confidence ≥ 0.7, reported by a test that prints the confusion per trait; a trait below the bar is shipped disabled in the catalog, not dropped from the code
Results are stored in a `glyph_traits` table (face, trait, value, scalar, confidence, detector version) with an index on (trait, value); a detector version bump recomputes only that trait

The trait pass runs in the background after the scan (like fingerprints), is cancellable, resumes after restart, emits progress through the `Event` enum, and never touches the first-scan budget: the 10k reference library completes the pass in under 60 s with the UI responsive
Variable fonts are measured at the default instance and the row says so; a later story may add instances

stories.title: Search by traits through fm-api, CLI and MCP
criteria: `fm-api` adds, additively, `SearchRequest.glyphTraits: Option<Vec<TraitFilter>>` (`#[serde(default)]`; a `TraitFilter` is trait id + wanted value, or a scalar range) and a `listGlyphTraits` request returning the catalog with per-value counts for the current library; no existing field changes (rule 6)

Search combines trait filters with every other filter and sort and stays under 50 ms on the reference library (the bench job checks it); fonts without the glyph are excluded from a trait filter, never counted as 'none'
`fm search --trait R.leg=straight --trait O.roundness>=0.95` works, and `fm traits` prints the catalog with counts
The MCP `search_fonts` tool accepts the same `glyphTraits` argument with the catalog in its description so an assistant can ask for 'a sans with a straight-legged R and a round O' in one call
`pnpm gen:types` regenerates types.ts with only additions

stories.title: The letters are the controls: shape pickers in the Letters preset
criteria: In the Letters preset the preview field renders the typed letters as individual letter buttons (20 px, Inter 500); a letter with traits in the catalog carries a 1.5 px hairline underline at 22 % ink, a letter without traits none; hover darkens the underline and shows the tooltip 'shape'; nothing else is added to the toolbar and nothing to the cards — matches dev-docs/design/redesign/8-letters-picker.png

Clicking an underlined letter opens a popover anchored under it: one radio per value showing the catalog's example glyph, the value label and the count of families in the current result ('312 families'), plus 'Any'; one value per letter (radio); Escape and outside-click close it; focus returns to the letter

A chosen value turns the letter's underline accent-coloured and adds an ordinary chip to the chip row ('R · leg · straight', glyph in semibold), removable there or by choosing 'Any'; chips persist when the preset is switched back to Word or any other, and the filter button's badge counts them
The filter popover gets no Letters group; the count line names active traits ('41 families · Sans serif · R leg straight · O round') — matches 8-letters-filtered.png

`R:straight O:round` typed in the search box parses to the same chips (and back), and the command palette gains 'Match by letters…' which switches to the Letters preset; e2e covers click letter → choose → chip → switch preset → chip remains → remove

stories.title: Letters: a wall preset that shows only the glyphs you type
criteria: The preset row (E41.2) gains Letters: the preview field takes glyphs ('ROga', any Unicode), and every card shows exactly those glyphs, large, centred, spaced evenly, in the family's default face; the size slider applies at 1.2×; cards of families missing a glyph show tofu for it (E43.4), never a fallback
With no glyphs typed the field hints 'Type the letters that matter — R O a g e tell faces apart' with those five as tap-to-add; the glyphs and preset are remembered per view
The Letters preset works with every filter including traits (E49.6) and with the language picker; sorting by name, date and the usual keys is unchanged
Matches dev-docs/design/redesign/8-letters-wall.png; the wall's 60 fps scroll budget holds with 1,000 families in Letters at 4 glyphs

stories.title: Trait tags on the Family page with 'find fonts with this'
criteria: The Characters section (E42.5) shows the family's detected traits as quiet tags under the glyph grid — 'R leg · straight', 'g · double-storey', 'O · round' — only those at confidence ≥ 0.7, in catalog order, each with its example glyph
Each tag has 'find fonts with this' (hover/focus); choosing it goes back to the wall in the Letters preset with that letter typed and that value chosen as a chip, keeping the wall's other filters
A family with no detected traits shows nothing (no empty heading); the tags are plain text for screen readers; Playwright covers tag → wall → chip present

stories.title: Later: per-glyph similarity in fm-core
criteria: Built after E49.1–E49.7 ship. `fm-core::glyphs::similarity` rasterises one glyph at 64 px (default instance, normalised to the em and centred), computes a shape descriptor (e.g. Zernike moments or a shape-context histogram — the ADR decides and records why), and stores it per (face, glyph) for the trait glyphs plus any glyph requested on demand, cached
`fm-api` adds, additively, `findSimilarGlyph { face, codePoint, limit }` returning faces ranked by glyph distance with the distance exposed; the whole-font `findSimilar` is untouched
A test asserts that for the labelled corpus the nearest neighbours of a straight-leg R are straight-leg Rs in at least 85 % of cases, so the descriptor agrees with the traits where both apply
A 10k-library query answers under 150 ms from cached descriptors; descriptors for the trait glyphs are computed in the background trait pass (E49.4) under the same budget

stories.title: Later: 'an R like this one' — sort the wall by a reference glyph
criteria: Built after E49.8. In the Letters preset each glyph on a card, and in the Family page's Characters section (E42.5) each glyph detail, offers 'Fonts with an R like this'; choosing it sorts the wall by glyph distance to that reference and shows a sort chip 'R like Inter' that is removable
The wall's count line reads 'sorted by R like Inter'; the reference glyph is shown in the chip; the sort combines with any filter including traits
The MCP `search_fonts` tool accepts `likeGlyph { face, codePoint }` so an assistant can ask for 'a sans whose a looks like Futura's but with a double-storey g' (trait + likeness in one call)
Playwright covers choose reference → sorted → remove chip restores the previous sort; a target image is added to board 8 when this story is picked up

epics.title: After the designers' test — legibility, targets, the split Layout, Characters, Sources, Foundries
epics.summary: Feedback from the first designers using the app at WMG, turned into one rule and a set of fixes. The rule: the toolbar never changes shape — view-specific controls live inside the view. The fixes: Layout becomes a split (the list stays on the left, the layout pane follows the cursor, ↑/↓ read the next font); Lines rows get a fixed chevron gutter so a family is seen as a family; the activation dot becomes a 24 px three-state control (off · session · permanent) that toggles session activation; every icon button is 28 px with a 16 px glyph, catalogs included (Download and Activate become icons); the Characters section scales its cells with the pane, draws a discreet grid, keeps descenders, shows glyph details in a popover that can be switched off and metrics only while Compare with… is on; Waterfall joins the Family page as a section; Sources in Settings becomes cards with watch, rescan and progress; a Foundries section in the sidebar, folded by default, lists normalised foundry names with counts and filters by one. Targets: dev-docs/design/redesign/9-split.png, 10-characters-*.png, 11-sources.png.

epics.title: Before launch, part one — right-click, tags, an exact language filter, one toolbar, Preview options, row actions, Similar
epics.summary: Seven things found while using the app before the public release; more pre-launch epics will follow. (1) Right-click shows the webview's own menu almost everywhere (Back, Forward, Reload on fonts; Emoji and Import passwords in text fields): only the Characters grid and the Foundries sidebar prevent it today. The app shows a menu only where it has one; text fields get Cut, Copy, Paste and Select all. (2) The Tags group in the sidebar lists every tag but a tag is only a drop target; filtering by tag needs the Filters popover. A click on a tag filters, and the popover keeps its tag filter. (3) The language filter keeps fonts that lack required letters. Cause, in crates/fm-core/src/coverage.rs: NEAR_MISS = 5, so a face that lacks up to five base characters of the chosen presets still passes. Serbian (Latin) differs from basic Latin by ten code points (Č Ć Đ Š Ž in both cases), so a face lacking four of the ten passes: the fixture Neuton-Light lacks Ć Đ ć đ and is kept (checked against its cmap). Decision (Goran, 17 Nov 2026): for a language, one missing letter disqualifies the font; whoever needs a font for a language needs all of its letters. Pasted text keeps today's allowance for now: a font lacking a few of its characters is still shown with what it lacks. (4) The catalog views (Google Fonts, Fontshare, the Adobe Fonts note) have their own toolbar: text buttons for the view mode and a plain search input, where the library has the segmented control with icons, SearchBox and the size slider; and the language of the pangram cannot be chosen there. (5) The Preview options popover is a plain column of fields; it gets a designed layout and loses Text colour, Background and Surface. Decision (Goran, 17 Nov 2026): previews always use the colours the theme defines. (6) The actions that appear at the right of a hovered row are small and their tooltips do not show (they are native `title` attributes; the app has no tooltip of its own), and the Similar icon, a lens with '≈' inside, does not read at 16 px. (7) The Similar panel does not say what it is, and its ranking lets in fonts that were never measured. Cause, in crates/fm-core/src/similar.rs and index/search/similar.rs: a face without a glyph fingerprint (an icon font has no Latin letters to draw) is still a candidate; every component it lacks counts as half alike, and its OS/2 weight and width class are the defaults (400, 5) that most fonts share, so such a pair reaches about 77% and outranks measured pairs, although the module comment says it never does. That is how Font Awesome is '71% similar' to a display serif. There is also no floor: the best N are shown however weak, and classification is all-or-nothing at 3 of 11 points, so an unrelated sans can tie with a sibling of the reference family.

epics.title: Before launch, part two — first-run setup, one-click catalog installs, automatic update checks
epics.summary: Two things for the first public release. (1) A new user starts with an empty library and three decisions that live in three places: which folders hold the fonts (one button in the empty state), whether to use the online catalogs (off, in the sidebar), and where catalog downloads go (asked in the middle of the first Install, CatalogInstall.vue, which proposes `<Documents>/Font Fu Fonts`). A first-run setup asks them once, in order, and leaves out every question that already has an answer. Decisions (Goran, 18 Nov 2026): the setup runs at first launch, not in the installer (the .dmg and the AppImage have no installer to ask in, and rule 5 wants the same on three systems); the user can add several font folders; the catalogs are asked about before their folder; Adobe Fonts is not part of it (the app cannot download from it); a catalog install goes into one folder per catalog, `<download folder>/Google Fonts/<Family>` and `<download folder>/Fontshare/<Family>`, so Install is one click with nothing to choose; families downloaded before stay where they are (rule 2). Today install_family writes to `<download folder>/<Family>` (family_folder in crates/fm-core/src/catalog.rs) and Settings.download_folder is None until the first Install. (2) Updates. ADR 0012 has the signed in-app updater; `Settings.check_updates_automatically` is off by default and found only under Settings → About; the check runs once at start, from the Pinia store (stores/updates.ts), and a found update opens the dialog at once. The app stays in the tray for days, so a check at start misses releases, and most users never find the switch. Decisions (Goran, 18 Nov 2026): the setup asks about the automatic check as its last step; with it on the app checks at start and once a day; an update found by an automatic check is announced quietly, never by a dialog over the user's work; nothing is installed while the app is in use without the user asking; a third level, off by default, downloads the update in the background and installs it when the user quits, and a major version still asks twice. That third level is an exception to ADR 0012's 'nothing installs until the user confirms', so the ADR is amended. The release address stays GitHub releases for now; it may move to the project's website later, or stay.

stories.title: Install when I quit: download in the background, install after the normal quit

with it on, a patch or minor update found by an automatic check is downloaded in the background into the app's cache folder and verified exactly as a confirmed install is (signature, and made for the announced version, ADR 0012); a refused package is deleted, reported once, and nothing is installed

the install runs only when the user quits the app (Quit in the menu or the tray, or closing the window with 'keep in tray' off), after the quit path every quit uses and only once; the app does not start again after this install; the same writable-folder probe as today runs before the download and before the install, and admin rights are never asked for (rule 4)

stories.title: Settings: three levels for updates
criteria: Settings → About replaces the 'Check automatically' switch with one control of three choices: Off; Tell me when there is an update; Download updates and install them when I quit. It sets the two settings and never shows a combination the API refuses
the third choice says in one line each: a major version always asks first; fonts activated for the session end when you quit, as they always do

epics.title: Duplicates — a module for cleaning up a large collection without losing anything
epics.summary: Today duplicates are one section of the Problems view, reached from Settings › Sources. Detection (E8.1, crates/fm-core/src/index/duplicates.rs) knows two cases: the same file at two paths, and the same PostScript name with the same version in files that differ. Resolution (E8.3) is 'Keep this one', one group at a time, with a fixed keeper rule: newest version, then the library folder, then the path. Three things are missing for a collection that grew over twenty years. (1) Two versions of one font are not found at all, because a group needs the same version; this is the most common case in an old collection. (2) Favorite, rating, notes, tags, collections and sets are stored per face (user_meta, face_tag, collection_face, set_face), so they stay on the copy that goes to the trash and the kept copy has none of them. (3) Thousands of groups cannot be decided one by one. The other font managers do not solve this either: Typeface groups by PostScript name and selects by format, location or folder; MainType ranks by version, variable, dates, glyph and character counts and file size; FontBase shows duplicates only on a family's page; Connect Fonts and FontAgent offer a search; RightFont skips a known PostScript name at import. None shows what differs between two copies, none carries the user's metadata to the kept copy, none works on whole folders, and none knows which languages a copy supports. This epic builds the module on what is there: the index, the hashes, the language coverage with its `locl` flag (crates/fm-core/src/coverage.rs), the OS trash (ADR 0009) and the undo log (resolution, resolution_move). The core decides everything: the levels of sameness, what differs between copies, the keeper policy with the user's languages, the merge of metadata, the overlap of folders, the plan of a cleanup and its undo. The app, the CLI and MCP show and apply it. Nothing is ever removed without the user's confirmation, removal means the OS trash, and a copy can also be hidden without touching its file (rule 2).

stories.title: Levels of sameness: identical files, the same version, another version
criteria: fm-api gains an additive request that lists duplicate sets; the types `DuplicateGroup`, `DuplicateCopy` and `KeepCopyRequest` do not change, and `list_duplicates` lists the groups it lists today (which copy it marks as keeper is E56.4's subject)

a set has one of three levels: `identical` (the same hash at different paths); `sameVersion` (the same PostScript name and the same version in files that differ, a set that also says whether its copies differ in format); `otherVersion` (the same PostScript name in files whose versions differ)

a file is listed once per font it duplicates: an identical set whose files all sit in one set of another level is not listed again, and a set with three versions of which two are the same file shows those two as identical inside it
versions are compared as today (digit runs as numbers); a copy without a version is its own value and is never called older or newer than another

a collection file (.ttc) with several faces is one copy per set it takes part in; a file that takes part in several sets says so, so that a plan never trashes it for one set while another set keeps it
only the files the library shows count (not gone, source not paused, read), as today; system font folders are listed and can never be chosen for removal (rule 4), and the answer marks such copies
the request takes a scope: the whole library, one source, or one folder with its subfolders; and it pages, so the UI never holds every set

the listing does not run at start and cold start stays under 1 s; scripts/bench.sh gains a number for the listing on the reference library with one of its folders copied beside it, the PR records it, and the ADR of this epic sets the budget from that number
MockApi and the TypeScript mock give the same sets for the same library; a test for each level, for the .ttc case and for a set of mixed levels
a new ADR, 'Duplicates', records the levels, why two versions are now a duplicate set, what is out of scope (fonts that only look alike), and the date (Goran, 20 Nov 2026)

stories.title: What differs between the copies
criteria: each copy of a set carries the facts a decision needs: path, source, format, version, file size, modified date, number of glyphs, whether it is variable and its axes, its OpenType features, whether the app activated it, whether a document asked for it (activation_document), and whether the user put a favorite, a rating, tags, notes, a collection or a set on it
each copy carries its languages from the index's coverage (the presets in data/charsets): which it covers in full, and for which it has `locl` forms; nothing is computed in the adapter or the UI

an additive request compares two copies of a set and answers in words a user reads: languages gained and lost, glyphs added and removed (the counts and the first of each), features added and removed, axes added and removed, and whether the vertical metrics, the units per em or the advance widths of shared glyphs changed

when the metrics or advance widths changed the answer says that text set in the other copy may reflow; when nothing but the container differs (the same outlines and tables in OTF and TTF or WOFF) it says so

the comparison reads the two files on demand and parses with fontations; a file that does not parse gives `Health::Broken` for that copy and a comparison that says which side could not be read, never a panic
a comparison of two faces of the reference library answers within the budget the ADR sets; the PR records the number
tests on fixtures/fonts: two versions where the newer adds a language, two where the newer loses glyphs, two with changed metrics, and one pair that differs only in format

stories.title: The languages you work in
criteria: the settings gain the languages the user works in: a list of preset ids from `list_languages`, empty by default, added with `#[serde(default)]`; an id that no longer exists is dropped on read and reported once
fm-api sets and reads the list; it is stored in config.json, never in localStorage
with the list empty every rule and guard of this epic that names 'my languages' does nothing, and the answer says that no language is set, so the UI can offer to set them
MockApi and the TypeScript mock follow; `pnpm gen:types` only adds lines

stories.title: Keeper policy: an ordered list of rules, with the language guard
criteria: the policy is an ordered list of rules stored in config.json through fm-api; a copy that wins a rule wins the set, a tie goes to the next rule, and the last rule is always the path A to Z so that the answer never depends on chance

the rules: covers more of my languages; has `locl` forms for more of my languages; newest version; format in an order the user sets (default OpenType CFF, TrueType, WOFF2, WOFF, Type 1); variable over static; most glyphs; in a folder the user prefers (an ordered list of folders); in the library folder; carries the user's metadata; active or asked for by a document

the default policy is: covers my languages, newest version, format, the library folder, path; with no language set it gives, for every set that `list_duplicates` also lists, the keeper that `choose_keeper` gives (a test over the fixtures)

the language guard is not a rule and cannot be turned off by the order: when a copy is the only one of its set that covers one of my languages in full, it is never recommended for removal; a set in which no copy covers everything the others cover is answered as 'keep both' with the languages each side alone has

every recommendation carries its reason as data (the rule that decided and the values compared), so the UI, the CLI and MCP say the same sentence: 'kept: covers Serbian Cyrillic, the other copy does not'
an additive request previews a policy without saving it: for a scope, how many sets get a keeper, how many are 'keep both', and how many recommendations change against the saved policy
the policy never applies to a copy in a system font folder, and never recommends removing the last copy of a font

`list_duplicates`, `fm doctor` and `list_problems` take their keeper from the saved policy and the guard (Goran, 20 Nov 2026), so the Problems view, the CLI and the module never recommend different copies of one set; no type changes: the keeper is still first and marked `keep`, and in a set answered 'keep both' every protected copy is marked `keep` and is no Problems entry; `choose_keeper` stays as the rule of the default policy with no language set
the ADR records the policy, its default, the guard and why it is not a rule, and that the keeper of the existing requests follows the policy from this version on

stories.title: Nothing you made is lost: the kept copy takes over the metadata
criteria: a test first shows today's behaviour: after `keep_copy`, a favorite, a rating, a tag, a note, a collection and a set put on the trashed copy are not on the kept copy; the PR records the result, and if the test shows they already move, this story shrinks to the cases below that fail

before a copy leaves the library (trash or hide), the faces of the kept copy take over what the user put on the matching faces of that copy; faces match by PostScript name, so a .ttc and loose files match face by face
tags, manual collections and sets are joined; favorite is on when any copy has it; rating, license and notes keep the kept copy's value when it has one and take the other's when it has none

where both copies have different ratings, licenses or notes, nothing is guessed: the plan lists the difference as a conflict with both values, the kept copy's value is the default, and the user can take the other one before applying; notes of the other copy are never dropped silently
the merge, the move and the undo log are one transaction: when the move fails, the kept copy's metadata is as it was

undo puts both sides back exactly: the restored copy has its metadata again and the kept copy has what it had before, also when the user changed the kept copy in between (what the user changed after the cleanup stays; only what the merge added is taken away)
the sidecars of both sources are written through the existing sidecar path (E7.3), so another machine that syncs the folder sees the merge and not a conflict
the merge runs for every resolution, `keep_copy` included (Goran, 20 Nov 2026): what an existing request does changes, no type changes, and the ADR records it
tests: each field alone, a conflict on each single-value field, a .ttc against loose files, undo after a later change, and a failed move

stories.title: Folders that hold the same fonts
criteria: an additive request lists pairs of folders that share copies: for folder A against folder B, how many of A's font files have a copy in B at each level, how many files A has in all, and the size of the shared files

a folder all of whose font files have an identical copy in the other folder is marked 'contained'; when every subfolder of a folder is contained in the matching part of the other tree, the pair is reported once at the highest such folder, not once per subfolder
pairs are ordered by the size that removing the smaller side would free; a pair below a threshold of shared files (set in the ADR, default five) is not listed; the request pages

the answer names for each pair what is only in A and only in B (counts, and the files through a second request), so the user sees what would be lost by treating the folders as the same; files that are not fonts are counted and never touched

a folder pair is a scope for the plan (E56.7): 'keep B's copies' plans the removal of A's files that have an identical copy in B and nothing else; copies of another level in the pair are planned only when the user asks for it and then go through the policy and the guard
a source root, a system font folder and the library folder can be the kept side and never the removed side as a whole
tests: a copied folder, a copied tree with one changed file, two folders that share a third of their files, and a folder contained in two others

stories.title: Plan, apply, undo: a cleanup as one session
criteria: an additive request plans a cleanup for a scope (the library, a source, a folder, a folder pair, or a list of sets) and a choice (the policy, or a keeper the user picked per set); it touches nothing and answers, per file, what would happen and why: move to the trash, hide, stays

the plan lists what it will not do and the reason: a copy the app activated (rule 3), the only copy that covers one of my languages, a set answered 'keep both', a copy in a system font folder, a file that takes part in another set that keeps it, a file that is not there any more

for an identical set the plan offers to move the activation to the kept copy (deactivate the one, activate the other, both the app's own registrations); for every other level an active copy stays, as today

the plan carries the metadata conflicts of E56.5 and the space it frees; a plan can be saved as JSON and applied later, and applying checks every file again against its hash, so a file that changed since the plan is skipped and reported

applying a plan creates one session with a name and a date; files go to the OS trash through `fm_platform::Trash` (ADR 0009), never `remove_file`; progress is sent through the typed `Event` enum (a new variant; nothing existing changes) and the apply can be cancelled between files, leaving a session of what was done

sessions are listed with what they did and can be undone whole or file by file; undo follows ADR 0009 (never over a file that is at the old path again; an emptied trash is reported per file) and puts the metadata back as E56.5 says

the resolutions of `keep_copy` appear as sessions of one set, so there is one history; the existing resolution tables are extended, not replaced, and an index from an earlier version opens with its resolutions listed
a plan for a thousand files on the reference library applies within the budget the ADR sets, and the library change is one `Event::LibraryChanged` per batch, not one per file
tests: a plan that mixes all outcomes, a file changed between plan and apply, cancel in the middle, undo of a whole session, undo after the trash was emptied

stories.title: Two outcomes that touch no file: hide a copy, and 'these are not duplicates'
criteria: a copy can be hidden: its file stays where it is, its faces leave the library, search and activation lists, and it stays hidden across scans and restarts; a hidden copy is known by its path and hash, so a different file at that path is shown again
hidden copies are listed through fm-api and can be shown again one by one or by session; a hidden copy that the app activated is refused with the same message as a move
hiding carries the metadata to the kept copy exactly as a move does (E56.5), and showing again undoes that as an undo does

a set can be answered 'not duplicates' or 'keep both': the decision is remembered for exactly these files (their hashes), the set is no longer listed or counted, and it comes back when a file of it changes or a new copy joins it
remembered decisions are listed and can be taken back; they are stored in the index and written to the sidecar of the family, so a synced folder carries them to another machine
a rebuilt index reads hidden copies and decisions back from the sidecars; a test for each: hide, show again, a changed file at a hidden path, a new copy joining a 'keep both' set, and a rebuild

stories.title: The same in the CLI and MCP
criteria: `fm duplicates list` (scope, level, `--json`), `fm duplicates folders`, `fm duplicates compare <a> <b>`, `fm duplicates plan` (scope, `--out plan.json`), `fm duplicates apply <plan.json>`, `fm duplicates sessions` and `fm duplicates undo <session>` are thin over fm-api: no rule is written in fm-cli
`apply` without `--yes` prints the plan's summary (files to the trash, hidden, skipped with reasons, space freed) and asks; it never deletes for good and has no flag that does
the human output says the reason of each recommendation in the sentence the API carries; `--json` is the API's answer unchanged

fm-mcp gains tools to list sets, list folder pairs, compare two copies and plan a cleanup; it has no tool that applies one (Goran, 20 Nov 2026: not for now), and the plan's answer says where the user applies it
`fm doctor` keeps the shape of its output, its keepers follow the policy (E56.4), and it gains one line that names `fm duplicates` when sets exist
tests against the binary for each subcommand on the fixtures; docs/user gains 'Cleaning up duplicates' with the CLI and what each level means

stories.title: Board: the Duplicates module
criteria: DESIGN.md gets a 'Duplicates (board 14, E56)' section: the module is a full view of its own with a 232 px navigation as in Settings (Overview, Folders, Sets, Plan, History, Hidden copies; the languages the user works in at its foot, with the link to the rules); where it is opened from (the 'Duplicates' row in the sidebar's Sources group, the notice after a scan, the 'copies' mark on a family, the command palette) and why it is not part of Problems: duplicates are housekeeping, not faults, so their count is neutral and never the red dot

the same section records: the three outcomes and their words (the trash of this system, Hide, Keep), 'Keep all' and 'Not duplicates' for a whole set; the recommended copy carries the accent ring and a 'Keep' badge and its reason is one sentence under it; a missing glyph in a specimen is the accent tofu marker (E43.4), never a fallback; nothing the guard protects is preselected for removal; the module uses no control the rest of the app does not have

dev-docs/design/redesign/ gains the exports of board 14 at 2×, one per state of `Duplicates.dc.html` (`14-duplicates-overview.png`, `-folders`, `-sets`, `-compare`, `-plan`, `-applying`, `-history`, `-hidden`, `-rules`) and `14-duplicates-entry.png`, with the README table and the export date updated; the dark theme follows DESIGN.md's rules, as for boards 1 to 11

before the export the owner confirms the four states and the entry sheet that were a first pass (Applying, History, Hidden, Rules, the ways in), and the UI stories are checked against the board once more

stories.title: The module: overview and the queue of sets
criteria: the module is a full view of its own (route `/duplicates`, like Studio) with the 232 px navigation of board 14: 'Library' to go back, then Overview, Folders, Sets, Plan, History and Hidden copies with their counts, and at its foot the languages the user works in with the link to the rules; the overview shows how many fonts have more than one copy, the extra files and the space a cleanup would free, and, while no language is set, one line that offers to set them
identical sets are offered as one decision ('1,240 identical copies in 3 folders') that opens the plan; the other levels are a queue the user works through
the queue is virtualized and pages through the API; it filters by level, source, folder, format, 'has a recommendation' and 'keep both', and sorts by name, size freed and number of copies

a set shows its copies with the recommended keeper, the reason as the API gives it, and each copy's version, format, folder and languages; the user can pick another keeper, choose hide, or answer 'keep both' or 'not duplicates'; the queue then moves on
every decision is collected into the plan and nothing moves until the plan is applied; the collected plan survives leaving the module and a restart (through fm-api, not localStorage)
the queue is keyboard-complete: next and previous set, choose a copy, each outcome, open the comparison; focus is never lost when a set leaves the queue

the component computes nothing about fonts; strings in en and de; the a11y and contrast specs pass; it matches the board within the tolerance REVIEW.md sets and moves per MOTION.md; a Playwright spec on the mock covers the overview, a decision of each kind and the filters

stories.title: The folders view
criteria: the view lists the folder pairs of E56.6, largest saving first, each with both paths, 'contained' or the share, and the size

a pair opens to what both have, what only one side has, and the copies that are not identical; 'Keep this side' adds the pair to the plan and says in one line exactly what that covers: the identical copies of the other side, nothing else
a side the API does not allow to be removed (a source root, a system font folder, the library folder) shows why and offers only to be kept
paths are shown in full on demand and can be opened in the file manager through the existing command; the list is virtualized
strings in en and de; keyboard-complete; a Playwright spec on the mock covers a contained pair, a partial pair and a refused side

stories.title: Comparing two copies
criteria: from a set the user opens two copies side by side: a specimen of each in the user's sample text, rendered by the webview through the asset protocol like the rest of the app, and the differences as the API states them

languages come first: what each copy covers of my languages, what one gains or loses against the other, and where only one has `locl` forms; the sample text can be switched to a language's sample so the difference is seen, not only named
glyphs added and removed are shown as glyphs, features and axes as lists, and changed metrics with the line that text may reflow
'Keep this one', hide, 'keep both' and 'not duplicates' are offered here as in the queue and act on the same plan

a copy that could not be read shows the API's message in its half; strings in en and de; keyboard-complete; a Playwright spec on the mock covers a language difference, a metrics change and a format-only pair

stories.title: Your languages and the keeper policy
criteria: the module offers 'Languages I work in': a picker over the presets of `list_languages`, with search, that saves through fm-api
the policy editor shows the rules in order; they are reordered by drag and by keyboard, turned on and off, and the rules with values (format order, preferred folders) open their own short lists
the language guard is shown above the rules as always on, with one line on what it protects; it is not a row that can be moved or turned off

while the user edits, the preview of E56.4 says how many sets get a keeper, how many are 'keep both' and how many recommendations change; nothing is saved until Save, and 'Back to the default' restores the default policy
strings in en and de; a Playwright spec on the mock covers setting a language, reordering by keyboard and the preview

stories.title: The plan, the sessions, and the ways into the module
criteria: before anything moves the plan is shown: files to the trash, files hidden, files that stay with the reason for each group of them, the metadata conflicts with both values and a choice, and the space freed; Apply names the number of files and the trash of this system
while a plan is applied the module shows progress from the events and a Cancel that stops between files; when it ends it says what was done and offers Undo
'History' lists the sessions with their date, what they did and Undo for the whole session or single files; a file that cannot come back (the trash was emptied, the path is taken) says so on its row
'Hidden copies' and 'Remembered decisions' list what E56.8 stores and take each back

the ways in, as on board 14's entry sheet: a 'Duplicates' row in the sidebar's Sources group with the number of fonts that have copies, in the neutral count style and never with the dot Problems uses, hidden while there are none; after a scan that finds copies, one notice in the app's notice style ('<folder> added · N fonts', how many are copies, Review, dismiss), once per scan, that never opens the module by itself; on a wall card and on the family page a quiet 'N copies' mark beside the style count that opens that font's set, and under Info › Files one line with 'Decide which to keep'; in the command palette 'Find duplicates' and 'Show the copies of <family>'

the Problems view keeps broken files, legacy formats and conflicts and shows one line with the number of duplicate sets that opens the module; its total and its dot no longer count duplicates; Settings › Sources links to the module instead of the Problems view; the old route `#/problems?kind=duplicates` opens the module

the UI subscribes to the events and does not poll; strings in en and de; the a11y and contrast specs pass; a Playwright spec on the mock covers a plan with a conflict, apply and cancel, undo of a session, and the three ways in
